recipe_steps.text: cook your choice of pasta in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until al dente.
Toast the grounded peppercorns until fragrant in a frying pan (with little butter) over medium heat, about 2 minutes. Keep them moving to prevent them from burning.

While the pasta cooks, add freshly grated parmigano cheese to the crushed black peppercorns on very low heat. Gradually add a cup of the boiling cooking water to the bowl, constantly mixing and adjusting as necessary to melt the cheese and obtain a silky, smooth sauce that’s able to completely coat the pasta. Finish with a knob of butter to emulsify the sauce
Once your cacio e pepe has become a creamy, silky sauce, add your piping hot pasta to the bowl and toss vigorously to coat.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Pour sugar from the sugar bowl into the pan filled with hot water.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding salt to the pasta water is a fundamental step for seasoning the pasta itself, which is essential for the final flavor profile of Cacio e Pepe.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using sugar instead of salt will sweeten the pasta, which is completely contrary to the savory, peppery, and cheesy nature of the dish, rendering it inedible.
mistake.why_observable_now: The ingredient is directly committed to the cooking water, which will be used later to emulsify the sauce.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the pasta has absorbed the sugar-water, it cannot be un-absorbed, and the cooking water is also used to create the sauce, spreading the sweetness throughout the entire dish.
mistake.why_plausible: Sugar and salt are both white granular substances often stored in similar containers in a kitchen, making it a common procedural slip.

recipe_steps.text: In a large bowl mix together flour, salt and then add oil. In a separate cup mix yeast with sugar in warm water. Pour over everything else and start kneading until the mix gets doughy and easy to work with. Using your hands rub the bowl with some oil and also rub some on the dough itself while keeping it as a big round shape then cover the bowl with plastic wrapping and a blanket and let it rest for about an hour.

STUFFING. Start preparing the meat stuffing. Sweat one chopped onion in a pot, for a few minutes and then add minced garlic, then place the meat in the pot and on high heat while continuing stirring let the meat cook until the red color turns into more brownish, the idea here is not to fully cook the meat, but perhaps to get all the water out, this will help to get rid of all the water residue that comes out of the meat so it can help the meat stick to the dough while baking.
Lower the heat, add some water if needed and a stock cube and leave for a total of 15 minutes.
Leave the stuffing to cool, then add a spoonful of yoghurt and another spoonful of tahini and a generous amount of sumac.

Heat oven on 200C (fan) and once the dough is ready, with your hands take a small piece of the dough and round it in a ball shape. Place in a greased tray, then flatten with your fingers (try not to flatten it too thin. it's nice to have it a bit fluffy once baked) with your fingers, scoop out some of the meat stuffing and place over the flattened dough, press well with hands to make sure the meat mixture sticks with the dough.

Continue this process until the tray is full, make sure there is some space between one sfeeha and the other, so they won't stick to each other while baking. After filling the dough with the meat mixture let it sit for another 10 minutes before baking.
Bake for about 8-10 minutes or until the bottom turns golden brown.

actions.text: Pick up the kettle from its base.
scratch the inner surface of the bowl on the countertop with the left hand removing a bit of dirt.
Pour hot water from the kettle into the bowl. This is the start of the prep for testing the yeast.
Put the kettle on the counter top. The kettle has not been returned to its base as it might still be used.
Pick up the water filter jug from the countertop.
Pour cold water from the jug into the bowl, trying to produce a lukewarm water for the yeast by mixing hot and warm water.
Put down the jug on the countertop.
Test the temperature of the water by dipping the pinky finger of the left hand in the water.
Pick up the water filter jug from the countertop.
Pour additional cold water into the bowl. The temperature was believed to be hotter than lukewarm, so more cold water is added.
Test the temperature again using the pinky of the left hand.
Put down the water filter jug.
Dry the left pinky finger by holding the end of the towel that is on the handrail of the oven.
Pick up the bowl with water from the countertop using both hands.
Pour some of the water into the sink. The water is still too hot and the bowl is nearly full. So emptying the current content to add more cold water.
Put down the bowl on the countertop.
Pick up the water filter jug from the countertop.
Pour additional cold water from the jug into the bowl.
Test the temperature of the water third time by dipping the pinky of the left hand into the water.
The water is believed to be acceptable at lukewarm temperature.
Put down the water filter jug.
Open the drawer using the right hand by pulling it.
Pick up a teaspoon from the cutlery tray inside the drawer.
Close the drawer.
Pick up a jar of sugar from the upper shelf on top of the sink using the right hand.
Open the jar of sugar by holding it with the left hand and holding the lid with the right hand and pulling it up.
Put down the lid of the sugar jar on the countertop using the right hand, flipping it upside down so as any sugar on the inside of the lid would not fall onto the surface of the countertop.
Scoop one teaspoon of sugar from the jar.
The jar is being held with the left hand, the spoon is with the right hand.
Pour the spoons content into the bowl with lukewarm water.
Scoop another spoon of sugar from the jar.
Pour the second spoon of sugar into the bowl with water.
Using the spoon in the right hand, mix the water with the sugar to dissolve it by moving the spoon in circular motions small and large clockwise.
Put down the sugar jar on the counter top.
Leave the spoon inside the bowl.
open the tin of yeast by holding the tin with the left hand, opening the lid by pulling it out with the right hand.
Pick up the tin of yeast from the countertop.
Put the lid on the countertop.
Open the cover of the jar by lifting the opener up using the thumb and then holding the opener and pulling it away. The jar is supported by the countertop surface during this.
Pick up the jar again from the countertop.
Take the spoon that's resting on the bowl.
Hit the spoon on the rim of the bowl a few times to remove excess liquid as it was soaked inside the water.
Scoop one full teaspoon of yeast from the jar.
Pour the yeast into the bowl.
Scoop another teaspoon of yeast from the jar.
Pour the yeast into the bowl.
Put down the jar on the countertop.
Mix the yeast with the water and dissolved sugar using the spoon by stirring the yeast in circular motions.
Using the left hand, pick up the lid of the jar from the countertop.
Attempt to close the jar but realize the lid is attached to it. So put the lid again on the countertop.
Push any remaining undissolved yeast onto the side of the bowl to help it dissolve with the spoon.
Mix again the content of the bowl by stirring. So all the yeast dissolves in water.
Hit the spoon on the rim of the bowl a few times to remove any stuck yeast on it.
Mix the content of the bowl again.
Hit the spoon again on the rim of the bowl.
discard the spoon in the sink, putting it inside one of the soaking bowls in the sink.
Pick up the lid of the yeast jar from the countertop.
Close the cover of the yeast jar. Try to put the lid on the cover realizing it's not possible, so put it again on the countertop.
Completely remove the cover of the jar.
Place the cover on the countertop.
Pick up the lid from the countertop.
Close the jar by covering it with the lid, holding the jar with the left hand and pushing the lid on top of the jar using the right hand.
Open the cupboard with the left hand using the handle.
Pick up a plate from a pile of plates on the lower shelf of the cupboard. Using the right hand, pick up the top plate from the pile.
Close the cupboard.
Cover the bowl with the plate by turning the plate upside down and placing it on top of the bowl. This seals the air from accessing the bowl by closing it.
pick up the cover discarded of the jar from the countertop.
open the lid of the trash bin
Throw the cover in the lid.
Close the lid, this action is off screen but you can hear it.
pick up the lid of the sugar jar from the countertop.
Close the sugar jar by turning the lid upright and pushing it on top of the jar using the left hand.
Pick up the sugar jar from the counter top.
Return the sugar jar on the upper shelf on top of the sink as its usage has concluded.
Open the lower cupboard.
pick up two large mixing bowls stacked on top of one another from the upper shelf of the cupboard. There is a plastic bag inside the inner bowl.
Hold the lower bowl in the stack using the left hand, then remove the upper smaller bowl from using the right hand.
Place the smaller bowl on the countertop.
Place the second bigger bowl also on the countertop.
Pick up a green bag of flour from the upper shelf of the cupboard.
Move a bag of pasta using the right hand inside the upper shelf of the cupboard to access a bag at the back.
Lift and inspect a blue bag of flour inside the upper shelf.
then return it back in the cupboard.
Close the cupboard.
Place the green bag of flour on the countertop between the two bowls.
Open the upper cupboard.
move a small glass on the second shelf of the cupboard to access a bigger glass behind it.
Pick up a glass from the second shelf of the cupboard.
Place the glass pointing up inside the upper bowl to use it to measure flour.
Pick up the green bag of flour from the countertop.
Open the bag by uncrumbling its opening.
Pour flour from the green bag into the glass inside the bowl to measure one cup of flour shaking the bag as needed to pour more flour from it.
Tilt the bag up once the cup is filled so as not to pour further flour.
pick up the filled glass of flour from the inside of the bowl.
Place the filled glass of flour next to the bowl.
Put down the bag of flour on the chopping board on the countertop.
Pick up the bowl from the countertop. Having realized it has some dirt, we'll clean the dirt before emptying the flour inside it.
Shake and dust the bowl on top of the sink using the right hand to remove any dirt from it.
hit the bowl on its back on top of the sink also to remove dirt.
Pick the glass filled with flour from the countertop.
put down the bowl on the countertop.
Empty the content of the glass into the bowl, now having measured one cup of flour.
Put down the glass on top of the pile of flour inside the bowl so as to measure more flour.
Pick up the green bag of flour from the countertop.
Pour more flour into the glass inside the bowl to measure a second cup of flour.
Pick up the glass.
pour the second cup of flour into the bowl now having measured two cups of flour.
Return the glass inside the bowl to measure more flour.
Fold the bag of flour that's now empty to discard it.
Open the lid of the trash bin.
Throw the empty green bag of flour in the bin.
Close the bin, this action is off screen.
Pick up the full red bag of flour that has been bought with the grocery from the countertop using both hands.
Place the bag of flour on the chopping board to open it.
Open the red bag of flour by unfolding its turned opening. tearing it.
Pick up the red bag of flour from the countertop, holding it using both hands. The right hand is supporting the base and the left hand is supporting the opening, so to pour from a limited opening.
Pour flour from the red bag into the glass that is inside the big bowl to measure a third cup of flour shaking it as needed to pour more flour.
Tilt the red bag up once the glass is filled to stop pouring flour.
Put the bag of flour on the chopping board on top of the counter top.
Close the bag of flour by folding its top a few times.
Pick up the filled glass of flour from the bowl.
Pour the flour from the glass into the bowl now measuring 3 cups of flour.
Shake and hit the glass on top of the bowl to drop any remaining flour from it into the bowl.
Turn the glass upright and place it on the chopping board on the countertop, having completed measuring flour.
pick up the bowl of flour, shaking it to spread the flour evenly inside it.
Put down the bowl of flour.
Open the upper cupboard using the left hand holding it from its handle.
Pick up the bottle of salt from the lower shelf of the cupboard.
Open the bottle of salt by flipping its cover.
Pour salt from the bottle into the bowl containing flour to add salt to the flour mixture.
close the bottle of salt by flipping the opening.
Put down the bottle of salt on the countertop having completed adding salt to the flour mixture.
Open the drawer using the left hand.
Pick up a spoon from the cutlery tray in the drawer.
Mix the salt with the flour using the spoon, holding the bowl with the left hand, and moving piles of flour and salt with the spoon using the right hand.
Pick up the smaller bowl from the countertop using the left hand. It has a plastic bag inside it.
Leave the spoon inside the bowl.
Open the lower cupboard.
Place the bowl on the upper shelf of the cupboard, returning it without using it.
Close the cupboard.
Hold the spoon again that's inside the bowl.
Mix the dry content of the bowl again using the spoon, holding the bowl with the left hand to steady it.
Pick up the bottle of olive oil from the shelf.
Return the bottle of vegetable oil that's being held in the left hand back on the shelf.
Move the bowl of flour and dry mixture slightly on the countertop.
Move the can of yeast on the countertop.
Put down the bottle of oil on the countertop.
Pick up the bowl of flour from the countertop.
Put down the bowl of flour on the countertop.
Hold the bowl using both hands. This is an attempt to pick it up but then change your mind.
Using the spoon, create a small gap in the flour to pour liquids.
Pick up the olive oil bottle from the countertop.
Open the bottle by holding it with the right hand, holding the lid with the left hand and rotating the lid counterclockwise.
Keep holding the lid with the left hand and pour oil from the bottle into the bowl that contains flour, pouring it in the center.
Close the bottle of oil.
Put down the bottle of oil.
Pick up the bowl containing water and yeast from the countertop using both hands.
Pour the content of the bowl into the bigger bowl with flour and oil, thus adding water, yeast and sugar into the mixture. These are the wet components of the dough.
Move the bowl upside down to ensure all the water inside it drop.
Put down the empty bowl on the countertop.
Using the spoon, mix the dry components, flour, and the wet components, water and oil.

Remove the part of the mixture that is stuck on the spoon using the fingers by sliding it. Hold two fingers against the spoon. Pass them through the surface of the spoon to remove the mixture stuck on the spoon.
Put the spoon on the empty bowl on the surface, discarding it.
Continue mixing the mixture by hand, trying to mix all the ingredients together in a homogeneous manner.
Pick up the water filter jug from the countertop using the left hand.
Pour a bit of water from the jug into the bowl with mixture. The dough needs a little bit more hydration.
Put down the water filter jug on the hob.
Mix the mixture into a dough, moving parts of it from the sides to the center and squeezing parts with fingers.
Pick up the water filter jug from top of the hob.
Pour a little more water into the bowl. The dough still needs more hydration.
Put down the water filter jug.
Continue mixing and kneading the dough.
Pick up the bowl with dough.
Place the bowl with dough on another countertop, giving more space to move the bowl.
Continue kneading and mixing the dough.
Knead the dough while turning the bowl. Knead and then turn the bowl slightly clockwise and then knead again and turn again continuously.
Open the bag of flour by unfolding its top.
Using the left hand, insert the hand into the bag and take a handful of flour from the bag.
Throw the handful of flour onto the dough mix. The dough is too wet, thus decreasing its wetness.
Combine the added flour with the dough by kneading and mixing.
Knead the dough while rotating the bowl clockwise.
Clear the hand from the stuck dough using the left hand scrape one finger at a time of the right hand to to get rid of the added dough and add it to the mixture
Continue kneading the dough, while turning the bowl clockwise.
Scrape the stuck dough on the right hand using the left hand by scraping one finger at a time.
Continue kneading the dough and turning the bowl clockwise.
Scrape the stuck dough on the hand using the other hand. One finger at a time.
Open the tap.
wash hands off the stuck dough using the water from the tap, scrubbing both hands against one another.
Close the tap.
Pick up the end of the towel hanging on the handrail of the oven and dry both hands.
Open the lower cupboard.
Pick up a smaller bowl from the upper shelf of the cupboard. The bowl has a plastic bag inside it.
Hold the bowl with the left hand, remove the plastic bag from inside the bowl, using the right hand.
Return the plastic bag to the upper shelf of the cupboard.
Close the cupboard.
On top of the sink, turn the the bowl upside down to empty some of the pink powder that has fallen inside it.
Turn the bowl upright and position it under the nozzle of the tap.
Open the tap.
Rinse the bowl.
Close the tap.
Open the tap.
Rinse the bowl again.
Close the tap.

Pick up the end of the white towel of the handrail of the oven and dry the inside of the bowl using the towel. The bowl is held with the left hand and the end of the towel with the right hand, moving it against the inner surface of the bowl.

Pick up the bottle of oil from the countertop.
Open the bottle of oil. The bottle is held with the right hand. Using the left hand, hold the lid and rotate it counterclockwise to open the bottle.
Hold the cap with the left hand, pour some oil from the bottle into the smaller bowl.
Put down the cap from the left hand onto the countertop.
Put down the bottle from the right hand on the countertop next to the bowl.

Using the right hand, spread the oil to the surfaces of the bowl to cover the inside surface, holding the bowl with the left hand to steady it. Oiling the bowl is to make it ready to put the dough inside it.
Using the right hand, gather the dough so as to pick it up from the bigger bowl.
Lift the bowl containing the dough and turn it upside down on top of the smaller bowl so as to slide the dough from it to the oiled bowl.
Slide the dough from the big bowl onto the small oiled bowl to prepare for its fermentation, using the right hand to assist in sliding any stuck parts of the dough.
Put down the empty large bowl on the countertop using the left hand.
Flatten the dough on the smaller oiled bowl using the right hand, by tapping it.
Pick up the olive oil bottle from the countertop using the left hand. Notice that the bottle is already opened so the lid is not on it.
Pour olive oil from the bottle into the smaller bowl on top of the dough to cover it with oil.
Spread the poured oil on the surface of the dough to cover it using the right hand, by moving the hand around the dough inside the small bowl.
Put down the oil bottle on the countertop using the left hand next to the empty bowl.
Rotate the small bowl using the left hand to help with spreading the oil evenly on the surface of the dough using the right hand.
Pick up the empty bowl from the countertop using the left hand.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Drop the beef stock cube inside the mug with hot water to melt it forming some stock using the left hand.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The recipe specifically calls for chicken stock to complement the meat stuffing for the Sfeeha, and the stock is a key flavor component.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using beef stock instead of chicken stock significantly alters the intended flavor profile of the Lebanese meat pies, which relies on the specific savory notes of chicken stock.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of dropping the cube into the mug is the point of commitment for the stock ingredient.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the cube is dissolved into the hot water, it cannot be removed or separated from the liquid, and the stock is then poured into the meat mixture, making it impossible to undo without discarding the entire stuffing.
mistake.why_plausible: Beef and chicken stock cubes often come in similar packaging and are stored in the same fridge or pantry area, making it a common human error to grab the wrong one.

recipe_steps.text: Start by mixing the melted butter, sweetened condensed milk with the cocoa powder. Combine them really well together, but it's okay if there are a few small lumps.
Crumble up the biscuit and combine with the mixture
It's important to use small sized biscuit crumbs like in the picture, but also try and incorporate really small crumbs in there as well to help the mixture hold
The last step is shaping the mixture. Do this by placing the mixture on a chopping board and shaping into a cylindrical log using the hands.
Next wrap the log with foil to help it maintain its shape and place it in the fridge for at least 5 hours (depending on your freezer)
After roughly 2 hours, divide into chunks of your desired thickness.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Pour the flour from the glass into the pot by holding the glass on top of the pot and tilting it so all the flour falls into the pan where the butter is.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits the dry ingredient to the butter base, which is a fundamental step in creating the chocolate sauce for the Lazy Cake.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding flour instead of cocoa powder ruins the flavor profile and the texture of the chocolate sauce, which is essential for the cake's binding and taste.
mistake.why_observable_now: The color difference between cocoa powder and flour is immediately apparent once the ingredient is poured into the melting butter.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the flour is mixed into the hot, melting butter, it cannot be separated, and the base for the sauce is permanently compromised.
mistake.why_plausible: The cook has several glasses and containers on the counter, and it is easy to mistake a glass of flour for a glass of cocoa powder if they are not clearly labeled.

recipe_steps.text: Heat butter in a pot over medium heat until the butter melts. Add onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4 to 6 minutes. Stir in carrots and mix until properly coated. Add water and broth; bring to a lively simmer over high heat.  Reduce heat to maintain a lively simmer and cook until very tender, about 25 minutes.
Puree the soup in batches in a blender until smooth. (Use caution when pureeing hot liquids.) Stir in spice mix and fresh coriander.

actions.text: Take one carrot out of the bag of carrots using the left hand.
Slightly move the bag of carrots on the countertop.
Put down the single carrot also on the countertop.
Open the lower cupboard.
Close the cupboard realizing what I'm looking there is not there. The cupboard does not close fully.
Open another lower cupboard.
Open the second door of the lower cupboard.
Pick up a plastic tupperware from the lower shelf of the cupboard using the left hand.
Close the cupboard's door.
Put the plastic tupperware on the countertop.
Pick up the peeler from the countertop.
Attempt to remove the plastic cover of the peeler's blade. I assume by the end of the attempt that this indeed is correct.
pick up the single carrot from the countertop.
Hold the carrot with the left hand, move the peeler down the skin of the carrot to peel it, realizing the peeler is not working, after a few attempts.
Try to figure out what's going wrong with the peeler, attempting to move its blade around.
Put down the carrot again on the countertop to figure out how to fix the peeler.
Keep fiddling with the peeler until I figure out how to remove the plastic cover of the blade.
Remove the plastic cover of the peeler by unhooking it from both ends.
Put the cover on the counter top.
Using the fingernail keep scratching the end of the blade so as to get the edge of this plastic cover covering the peeler, This attempt is repeated a few times as it's not successful.
correctly get the edge of the cover using scratching the nail of the peeler.

pull away the cover on top of the peeler having finally caught its end. The peeler is being held with the right hand and the cover, the plastic cover, which is transparent and blue using the left hand.
Open the trash bin.
Throw the plastic cover.
Close the trash bin.
Pick up the carrot from the countertop using the left hand.

Hold the carrot with the left hand, peel skin of the carrot by holding the peeler against the carrot using the right hand and sliding it down the length of the carrot to peel it, continuing this several times, while rotating the carrot with the left hand to access all its sides, As the carrot is positioned on top of the plastic bowl, the peel is falling into the bowl.
Put down the peeled carrot on the chopping board to the left of the bowl.
Pick up a second carrot from the plastic bag.

Position the carrot on top of the bowl so the peel falls into the bowl. Again, peel the skin off the carrot by holding the carrot with the left hand, holding the peel with the right hand, and then pushing and sliding the peel along the edge of the carrot to peel it, rotating it with the left hand so all its sides are peeled, continuously sliding the peel across the length of the carrot.
Put down the peeled second carrot.
Pick up the third carrot from the bag.

Peel the third carrot. Position the carrot on top of the bowl so the peel falls into the bowl. Again, peel the skin off the carrot by holding the carrot with the left hand, holding the peel with the right hand, and then pushing and sliding the peel along the edge of the carrot to peel it, rotating it with the left hand so all its sides are peeled, continuously sliding the peel across the length of the carrot.
Put down the peeled third carrot.
Pick up the fourth carrot from the bag.

Peel the fourth carrot. Position the carrot on top of the bowl so the peel falls into the bowl. Again, peel the skin off the carrot by holding the carrot with the left hand, holding the peel with the right hand, and then pushing and sliding the peel along the edge of the carrot to peel it, rotating it with the left hand so all its sides are peeled, continuously sliding the peel across the length of the carrot.
Put down the fourth carrot on the chopping board after being peeled.
Pick up the fifth carrot from the bag. The hand needs to access deeper into the bag this time to get this carrot.
Peel the fifth carrot using the same method.
Put down the peeled fifth carrot on the chopping board.
Shake the peeler on top of the Tupperware to get rid of some of the peel that had stuck to it.
Pick up the sixth carrot from the plastic bag using the left hand.
Peel the sixth carrot in the same way.
Shake the peeler on top of the Tupperware to get rid of some of the stuck peel to it.
Put down the peeled sixth carrot on the chopping board. Piling the carrots now that have been peeled.
Pick up the seventh carrot from the bag using the left hand.
Peel the seventh carrot using the same method. During peeling this carrot as its shape is different than the others, it's not straight, the peeler is struggling to reach the end of the carrot.
Touch the left hand using the right hand as the peeler had slightly touched the hand with its blade, potentially injuring it, but no harm has been done.
Turn the carrot upside down in an attempt to make the peeling easier due to the odd shape of the carrot.
Try to peel the carrot upside down, moving the peeler against its length. Again, the odd shape of the carrot is making peeling this particular carrot difficult.
Put down the peeled seventh carrot on the countertop.
Shake the peeler on top of the tupperware to get rid of some of the stuck peel to it.
Reach into the bag of carrots to get the next carrot, then look back at the meat.
Pick up the lid of the pan using the left hand. You can see steam coming out of the meat being cooked.
pick up the wooden spoon using the right hand. This action is mostly off screen, only its shadow is visible.
Place the lid onto the other pan on the hob, again in an effort to not let the steam in the pan drip on any surface.
Stir the meat in the pan by turning it upside down and also moving the wooden spoon inside the meat.
Rest the wooden spoon on the pan and the meat.
pick up the mug containing chicken stock after dissolving the stock cube into the water from the countertop next to the hob.

Pour the stock from the mug to the pan by holding the mug on top of the pan and tilting it for the liquid inside it to pour into the pan and moving the mug around while doing so to spread the water around the pan.
Put down the empty mug on the countertop, discarding it.
pick up the wooden spoon that was resting on the pan.

mix the chicken stock that has been poured into the pan with the pan's content. Some of the chicken stock has not dissolved fully, so it can be visibly seen. So, mixing also that with the meat, holding the handle of the pan with the left hand and moving it, rotating it to access all the pan's content.
Hit the wooden spoon on the rim of the pan to drop any content of the meat that has stuck to it.
pick up the lid from the hob.
Put down the wooden spoon on the plate next to the hob.
cover the pan again with the lid, allowing it to continue to cook with the left hand, The pan is slightly sliding off the rim, so fixing it carefully to be stable.
scratch the nose
Pick up the eighth carrot from the bag using the right hand
Move the carrot from the right hand to the left hand.
Pick up the peeler from the countertop.
Peel the eighth carrot in the same way.
Hold this carrot, turn it 180 degrees and peel its top end, rotating it. This is different to how other carrots have been peeled. This is done in short strokes of the peeler.
Put down the 8th peeled carrot on the chopping board.
Pick up the ninth and final carrot from the bag. The right hand has to hold the bag as it's now empty and doesn't have any weight to get the carrot using the left hand from inside it.
Peel the ninth carrot by holding it, turning it 180 degrees and peeling its top end, rotating it.
Put down the ninth carrot on the chopping board.
Shake the peeler on top of the plastic tupperware to get rid of stuck peel to it.
Pick up a very small remaining cut out from the bag using the left hand.
Peel the last small tenth carrot by hold ing it, turning it 180 degrees and peeling its top end, rotating it
nouns: last small tenth carrot top end

actions.text: Rotate the carrot 180 degrees to peel it in the other direction as it's small and struggling to keep hold of it, peeling it in short strokes.
Rotate again 100 degrees and continue peeling its end.
Hit the peeler against the edge of the tupperware to get rid of any remaining peel that is stuck to it.
Put down the tenth carrot on the pile of carrots on top of the chopping board using the left hand.
pick up a pan that is empty and on the hob.
pick up the scale from the top of the microwave using the right hand.
Move the scale to the left hand so the left hand is now holding both the scale and the pan.
pick up the empty bag of plastic that used to have carrots from the countertop.
Move the peeler on the countertop, emptying space for the scale.
Put down the scale on the countertop.
Put the pan on top of the scale.
Open the trash bin's lid.
Throw the empty plastic bag into the bin.
Close the lid of the trash bin, this action is mostly off screen.
Press the button on the scale to switch it on.
Pick up the bottle of vegetable oil from the countertop next to the hob.
Close the bottle by holding the lid with the finger and pressing it in. We only see the beginning of this action, but hear the sound at the end.
Put down the bottle on another part of the countertop.
Open the fridge.
pick up butter from the third shelf of the fridge.
move a jar of chocolate in the second shelf of the fridge to the right to access behind it.

get another packet of butter from the second shelf of the fridge. The first packet has been opened a while ago, so only a little bit is left. This second packet might be needed to weigh the needed butter for the recipe.
Close the fridge.
put down the second complete package on the countertop.
Open the first package by uncrumbling the packaging, accessing the butter inside.
Using the right hand slide the remaining butter from the package having unwrapped it into the pan.
Crumble the empty packaging of butter.
Open the trash bin's lid.
Throw the empty packaging into the lid. This action is mostly off-screen.
Close the lid, this action is offscreen.
Open the first drawer.
Pick up a knife from the cutlery tray in the drawer using the right hand.
Unpack the second butter holding the packaging with the left hand and unfolding the edges with the right hand.
put down the butter on the countertop so as to take a slice from it.
Using the knife, slice into the butter, cutting from one end of the butter's rectangle.
Push the cut part using the knife to separate it from the rest of the butter. As the knife has not sliced the butter fully, this additional force causes the slice to separate from the soft butter.
Pick up the butter from the countertop.
Using the right hand, separate the slice from the packaging.
Drop the additional slice in the pan and check the weight.
Put the knife on the countertop.
Wrap the packaging of the butter to close it.
Put down the butter on the counter top.
Pick up the pen from the top of the notepad.
Write down the measurement of the butter on the notepad.
Slightly move the notepad on the countertop.
put down the pen on the notepad.
Slide the pile of peeled carrots from the chopping board onto the countertop.
pick up and move the remaining carrots from the chopping board, put them on the countertop.
pick up the knife from the chopping board.
Pick up the chopping board using the left hand.
Open the lid of the food trash bin.

Using the knife, slide the peel of the garlic that is on the chopping board into the food trash bin, by brushing the knife onto the chopping board. The sound heard is the sound of the edge of the knife on the chopping board.
Close the lid of the food trash bin.
Put down the chopping board on the countertop.
Pick up half an onion, that had been peeled earlier from one chopping board and placed on the other chopping board.
Slightly move one carrot off the chopping board.
slice the onion vertically, using the knife into thin slices, holding the onion with the left hand, slicing with the knife and moving the hand slightly as more slices are chopped.
Reassemble the slices back into shape and rotate the onion 90 degrees in order to slice it in the other direction.
Now slice the onion in the other direction horizontally using the knife into thin slices.
Using the edge of the knife, slide the onion slightly to the right to empty space for chopping the other half onion.
Pick up another half onion already peeled a while back using the left hand from the chopping board.
Using the right hand, remove one onion skin that was attached to the half onion and drop it on the chopping board.
Using the edge of the knife, move all the already cut onion pieces to empty space for the newly added half onion.
slice the onion into slightly thicker slices than before by holding the onion with the left hand and slicing with the right hand on the knife. The slices are indeed thicker than the previous version.
Hold the cut onion and rotate it 90 degrees to slice it in the other direction.
slice the onion horizontally using the knife.
Again, slide the onion pieces using the knife on the chopping board to empty space for additional cutting.
Pick up a third half of onion that had been peeled before from one chopping board.
Put it back on the other chopping board.
pick up one onion piece that had fallen off onto the countertop and return it to the chopping board using the right hand that is also holding the knife.
Slice the third half onion vertically using the knife.
Hold the cut slices using the left hand and rotate 90 degrees to slice horizontally.
Slice the third onion horizontally using the knife. Due to the small size and speedy performance, the pieces now are a lot bigger.
Put down the knife on the chopping board.
Pick up one piece of onion that has fallen onto the floor using the right hand.
collect more onion pieces that have fallen onto the countertop using both hands, and put these on the chopping board to be thrown.
pick up the chopping board containing onion peel and pieces to be discarded, using both hands.
open the lid of the food waste bin using the right hand.
slide all the onion peel from the chopping board onto the bin using the right hand.
Close the lid of the food waste bin.
put down the empty chopping board on the countertop.
Open the cupboard.
Pick up a jar of spices from the lower shelf of the cupboard using the right hand.
Put down the jar of spices on the countertop next to the hob.
Pick up the lid on top of the pan containing meat using the left hand. You can see the steam coming out of the pan once the lid is lifted.
place the lid on the other hob.
pick up the wooden spoon from the plate on the countertop using the right hand.
Stir the content of the pan using the wooden spoon.
Hit the wooden spoon on the rim of the pan to remove any meat that stuck to it.
Put down the spoon on the plate.
Pick up the jar of spices, from the countertop.
Open the jar of spices by holding the jar with the right hand, holding the lid with the left hand, and rotating the lid counterclockwise.
Hold the lid upside down with the left hand and put the jar on top of the lid, holding it also with the left hand.
Insert the right hand into the jar of spice and take a pinch of spice from the jar.
Sprinkle the spices onto the meat in the pan using the right hand, moving the hand around the pan, sprinkling the spices that have been pinched from the jar.
Insert the hand again into the jar. Take another pinch of spices.
Sprinkle the spices again on the meat in the pan.
Rub the fingers quickly against one another to drop any spice that has stuck to the hand.
Hold the jar with the right hand.
Turn the lid upside down, place it on the jar and close the jar by rotating the lid clockwise using the left hand.
Open the cupboard.
Return the closed jar onto the lower shelf of the cupboard using the right hand.
Close the cover, this action is off screen.
Pick up the wooden spoon from the plate.
Stir the content of the pan, mixing the spice with the meat, using the wooden spoon, moving all the meat and the spices around to mix fully, in all directions.
Hit the wooden spoon against the rim of the pan to drop any meat that stuck to it, rotating it a few times 180 degrees while hitting.
Put the wooden spoon on the plate.
pick up the lid from the other burner using the left hand.
Cover the pan with the meat with the lid so it continues cooking.
Open the tap.
wash the hands under the water by rubbing them against one another to get rid of any spice that had stuck to the hand while sprinkling the spices.
Close the tap.
shake the hands on top of the sink to drop any excess water.
Holding the edge of the towel that is on the handrail of the oven, dry both pans.
Open the upper cupboard using the left hand holding the handle.

Pick up a plate from the pile of plates in the lower shelf of the cupboard. As the plate is the second in the pile, the left hand is holding the plate at the top while the right hand slides the green plate out of the pile.
Remove the pan from the scale, holding the handle and putting it away, on the countertop. The pan has the measured butter.
Put the plate on the scale. In doing so the bottle of olive oil is moved a little to fit the space.
press the button on the scale to switch it on.
Pick up the chopping board containing chopped onion using both hands.
Pick up the knife from the chopping board.

Slide the chopped onion from the chopping board onto the plate using the knife. The knife scrapes the surface of the chopping board, thus pushing the onion pieces onto the plate in multiple turns in order to measure the amount of onions.
Remove one of the onion pieces from the plate using the hand to discard it.
Pick up an onion piece from the chopping board with skin on it. Free the skin from it using fingers and then add it to the plate.
Pick up another onion piece from the chopping board and add it to the plate.
Read the measurement of the scale. This is the weight of the onion.
Put down the chopping board on the countertop.
Put down the knife on the chopping board.
pick up the pen from the top of the notepad,
Write down the weight of the onion onto the notepad.
Put down the pen.
Pick up some onion pieces and skin from the countertop and the chopping board using both hands.
open the lid of the food waste bin.
throw these pieces into the bin.
Close the lid of the food waste bin. This action is off screen.
pick up the knife from the chopping board.
Take one carrot from the pile of peeled carrots using the left hand.
Place the carrot on the chopping board, holding it firmly with the left hand to prepare for cutting its end.
Cut one end of the carrot using the knife in one quick slice.
Turn the carrot around to cut the other end.
Cut the other end of the carrot using the knife. The cut end actually jumps and rolls onto the floor of the kitchen.
Follow the rolling piece of carrot end on the floor.
Pick up the carrot end that has fallen on the floor using the right hand. Notice the right hand is also holding the knife.
Pick up the other end that's on the chopping board using the left hand.
Place both ends on the counter top.
Cut the carrot into medium sized slices using the knife starting from one end until the other end, moving the left hand that's supporting the carrot while slicing.
Move the cut carrot pieces to the corner of the chopping board to free the middle part of the chopping board for cutting further carrots.
Pick up the second carrot from the pile of carrots. Place it on the chopping board, holding it firmly with the left hand.
Cut the narrow end of the carrot using the knife.
Turn the carrot around to cut the other end.
Cut the other end of the carrot using the knife.
Pick up both ends of the carrot using the right hand.
Place both carrot ends on the countertop, out of the chopping board, so that they are discarded.

starting from the thick end of the carrot, slice the carrot from one end to the other using the knife, moving the knife across the length of the carrot and sliding the left hand supporting the carrot until the carrot is fully sliced into medium sized slices.
Put down the knife on the chopping board.
Pick up the pan containing butter from the countertop, holding the pan from its handle.
turn on the top right burner of the hob by holding the second knob on the hob, pressing it down to ignite the burner and rotating it counterclockwise to switch it on.
Move the pan at the far end of the hob slightly to free space.

move the pan with meat from the first burner, that is the bottom right, to the top right to get it away from the edge of the hob. This way the meat continues to cook on the far burner while the close burner can be used for preparing the carrot soup.
Place the pan with butter on the bottom left burner of the hob.

adjust the heat on the bottom right burner, the one where the pan with the butter is, by increasing the temperature, rotating the knob with the right hand clockwise. The heat needs to be higher to melt the butter.
adjust the positions of both the pan and the pot slightly, holding both from their handles, the pan with the left hand and the pot with the right hand.
Slightly adjust the lid on the pan containing meat using the left hand.
Open the first drawer.
Close the drawer. This action is off screen.
Pick up the wooden spatula from the drainer using the right hand.
Put the wooden spatula on the plate to prepare for it to be used for the carrot soup. Now the butter needs to be melt before we add anything to the pan.
pick up the knife from the chopping board.
pick up another carrot from the pile of peeled carrots using the left hand.
position the carrot on the chopping board to prepare to cut the thick end of the carrot, holding the carrot with the left hand.

Chop the narrow end of the carrot.
Pick up both ends of the carrot using the right hand that's also holding the knife.
Place both ends on the countertop out of the chopping board to prepare to discard them.
move one piece that has fallen into the hole of the chopping board and place it on the chopping board using the right hand.

starting from the narrow end of the carrot, holding the carrot firmly with the right hand, slice the carrot into medium sized slices, from the narrow end to the thick end, using the knife, going across the carrot's length, and moving the left hand while doing so, as more pieces are cut.

put down the knife on the countertop supported by the chopping board.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits a dry ingredient into the melting butter base, which is a foundational step for the chocolate sauce.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding ground coffee instead of cocoa powder fundamentally changes the flavor profile of the sauce, making it bitter and unsuitable for the intended dessert.
mistake.why_observable_now: The ingredient is poured directly into the pot, making the substitution immediate and irreversible.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the coffee grounds are mixed into the hot, melting butter, they cannot be separated, and the entire batch of sauce would need to be discarded.
mistake.why_plausible: Ground coffee and cocoa powder can look very similar in a glass container, especially in a busy kitchen environment where multiple ingredients are being prepared.

recipe_steps.text: The meat: Sweat one chopped onion in a pot, for a few minutes and then add minced garlic, then place the meat in the pot and on high heat while continuing stirring let the meat cook until the red color turns into more brownish, the idea here is not to fully cook the meat, but perhaps to get all the water out, this will help to get rid of all the water residue that comes out of the meat.
Lower the heat, add some water if needed, a stock cube, cinamon, and additional pepper and leave for a total of 15 minutes.

The rice: start by soaking the rice in some room temperature tap water, with some salt, for at least 2 hours. Once soaking period is over, rinse the rice well until water runs clear to get rid of any excess starchiness.

The vermicelli: heat enough oil to coat the bottom of a large saucepan over medium high heat. Once hot, add the broken vermicelli strands, and continue to saute constantly until the vermicelli turns a golden brown. You have to be careful, because vermicelli can burn quite easily. At this point, your rice should be rinsed and ready to add because as soon as the vermicelli is ready, dump in the rice to prevent further cooking of the vermicelli strands. Stir with a wooden spoon to combine well. Add one cube of chicken cube, loosely divided into smaller chunks. then add the water.
The water: I like to go with a ration of 1 cup of basmati rice to 1.5 cups of water. Importantly, the water should cover the rice with an additional couple of centimetres.

Let the mixture come to a boil, then cover with a tight fitting lid and let it simmer at low heat for an additional 15-20 minutes or until water is fully absorbed. Then, remove from heat, and let stand an extra 10 minutes before fluffing.
Finish: Add the pre-prepared minced meat to the rice. Mix thoroughly.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The stock cube provides the primary seasoning and flavor profile for the rice and vermicelli mixture.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using beef stock instead of chicken stock fundamentally alters the intended flavor profile of the Vermicelli Rice with Meat dish, which is traditionally prepared with chicken or vegetable stock.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of adding the wrong stock cube is a direct, observable commitment of an ingredient to the liquid base.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the stock cube is dissolved into the hot water, it cannot be removed or separated from the liquid, and the entire liquid base would need to be discarded and remade.
mistake.why_plausible: Beef and chicken stock cubes are often packaged similarly and stored in the same location, making it easy to grab the wrong one during a busy cooking process.

goal: prepare Marinated Chicken with Soy Sauce

recipe_steps.text: Mix all the ingredients except for the chicken. Pour into a large container and add the chicken thighs.
Add water to cover.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Prepare for baking by adding the marinade and chicken. Cover with oil. Add chunks of chicken cube for additional taste
Bake until well browned and cooked through, about 1 hour at 350 degrees F, basting the tops often.

mistake.original_action_text: Tilt and shake the jar on top of the bowl where chicken and marination has been put. Shaking the jar to sprinkle some of the oregano from the jar into the chicken, moving the jar around to distribute the oregano. The jar is being shaken very quickly and with force.
mistake.llm_original_action_text: Tilt and shake the jar on top of the bowl where chicken and marination has been put. Shaking the jar to sprinkle some of the oregano from the jar into the chicken, moving the jar around to distribute the oregano. The jar is being shaken very quickly and with force.
mistake.mistake_action_text: Tilt and shake the jar of cinnamon on top of the bowl where chicken and marination has been put. Shaking the jar to sprinkle some of the cinnamon from the jar into the chicken, moving the jar around to distribute the cinnamon. The jar is being shaken very quickly and with force.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits a spice to the marinade, which directly alters the flavor profile of the chicken.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding cinnamon instead of oregano will drastically change the flavor of the savory soy sauce chicken marinade, making it unpalatable for the intended recipe.
mistake.why_observable_now: The addition of the spice is a direct, observable action that changes the composition of the marinade in the bowl.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the spice is sprinkled and shaken into the liquid marinade and onto the chicken, it cannot be removed or separated from the mixture.
mistake.why_plausible: Cinnamon and oregano jars are often similar in size and appearance in a spice rack, making it a common human error to grab the wrong one while distracted.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding water to a mixture of butter and dates while heating changes the consistency and chemical composition of the base for the date balls, which should be a dry, sticky paste.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: The recipe requires the dates and butter to form a thick, sticky binder for the biscuit crumbs. Adding water will prevent the mixture from setting properly when cooled, resulting in a runny or mushy texture that cannot be rolled into balls.
mistake.why_observable_now: The addition of water is a direct modification to the cooking process of the primary binding agent.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once water is incorporated into the hot butter and date mixture, it cannot be removed. The only way to fix it would be to evaporate the excess water by cooking it longer, which would likely burn the dates or change their flavor profile significantly.
mistake.why_plausible: It is a common mistake to add liquid to a pan when trying to soften ingredients or prevent sticking, even if it is not called for in the recipe.

recipe_steps.text: Microwave potatoes for 4-6 minutes until just soft
Cut the potatoes into chunks
When ready to serve, heat 6-8 tbsp sunflower or olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan until you can feel a strong heat rising.
If your pan isn't large enough, fry the potatoes in two batches - rather than crowding them. Have kitchen paper ready to drain them on. Add the potatoes in a single layer, not too tightly packed.
Turn the heat to medium-high, so that the potatoes sizzle, but don't stir until they start to brown underneath.
Turn them all evenly 2 or 3 times until nicely browned all over - this can take about 7 mins.
Then lift out with a fish slice or large spoon. Sprinkle with sea salt.

recipe_steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan, add bacon and cook, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked to your liking (3-4 minutes for semi-crisp).
In another pan, add remaining oil, crack eggs into a measuring jug, add some milk and beat them. Add pepper to taste
Once the eggs have been mixed, cook them over medium-high heat to your liking (3-4 minutes for a soft scramble).
Whilst the eggs and bacon continue cooking, shred cheddar cheese into a bowl.
Season the eggs with salt and add paprika if desired.
To serve, cut the baguette in half and butter both sides. Add the bacon, scrambled eggs, and cheese.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The oil is the cooking medium required to fry the bacon and eggs; substituting it with a high-acid liquid like balsamic vinegar fundamentally changes the cooking process and flavor profile.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Balsamic vinegar will caramelize and burn rapidly at frying temperatures, ruining the flavor of the bacon and eggs and preventing them from frying properly.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the liquid into the pan is a direct commitment of an ingredient to the cooking vessel.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is in the hot pan, it will immediately begin to reduce and coat the surface, making it impossible to remove without discarding the pan's contents and cleaning the pan.
mistake.why_plausible: Balsamic vinegar and olive oil bottles are often stored in similar containers or locations in a kitchen, making it a common slip to grab the wrong bottle.

goal: prepare Raspberry and Lemon Curd Tarts

recipe_steps.text: Thaw puff pastry for 1 hour in room temperature, until defrosted, or in the refrigerator overnight.

Prepare the Lemon Curd. Heat a bainmarie on medium-low heat. Add butter and wait for it to melt. Then add lemon juice, zest, raspberry juice, sugar, and eggs and whisk together until sugar melts into the mix and stir continuously. The lemon curd should begin to thicken and small bubbles will begin to form on the surface, about 40 minutes. Remove from heat once the lemon curd is thick enough for the whisk to leave marks on the surface.
In the meantime, prepare the puff pastry. Roll out the puff pastry to about 10 inches by 14 inches, then cut into squares.
Bake at 200 degrees C for 15 minutes, until the pastry is puffed. Cool for 3 minutes.
Layer the cooled raspberry lemon curd onto the top of the tart. Serve immediately. Store any leftovers in the refrigerator.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Sprinkle the granulated sugar from the right hand evenly across the puff pastry.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits a specific ingredient to the puff pastry surface, which is a key step in preparing the savory tart filling.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: The recipe calls for cheese to create a savory tart; adding sugar instead creates a flavor profile mismatch that ruins the intended dish.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of sprinkling the ingredient directly onto the pastry is the point of commitment where the wrong ingredient is introduced to the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the sugar is sprinkled and potentially pressed into the puff pastry, it cannot be removed without discarding the entire pastry sheet.
mistake.why_plausible: Sugar and shredded cheese are both granular or shredded ingredients often stored in similar bags or containers in a kitchen, making it a common slip.

recipe_steps.text: heat oven to 220c/fan 200c/gas 7.
Unroll a puff pastry, scatter over a couple of handfuls of grated Parmesan and then grate over the cheddar cheese, then fold in half.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out to the thickness of a 1 pound coin. Cut into 1cm strips, then twist the strips 3-4 times.
Lay on a baking sheet, scatter over more cheese and bake for 12 mins, or until golden.
Leave to cool, then keep in an airtight container for up to 2 days.

recipe_steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees C, fan 180 degrees C, gas 6. Line a large roasting tray with baking paper, remove the stalks from the mushrooms and place them on the tray.
Whisk together the coriander, cumin, ginger, chilli powder, nutmeg, paprika, salt and olive oil with the juice of 1/2 lemon. Drizzle this over the mushrooms and toss to coat.
Sit the mushrooms stalk-side down and cover with another sheet of baking paper. Weigh down the mushrooms with another empty baking tray and roast for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely dice the tomatoes and finely slice the red onion. Mix with the zingy lemon juice and season well. Set aside.
When the mushrooms are roasted drizzle them with the sugar syrup, garlic paste, and worcestershire sauce. Roast again for 15 minutes.
Halve each kebab wrap and warm in a griddle pan.
On each wrap pile on the tomato salad for crunch followed by the sliced mushrooms. Drizzle the kebabs with the yogurt or aioli, if using, grated parmesan, and chilli sauce to taste.

mistake.mistake_action_text: pour and scrape the sugar into the bowl.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding salt is a key seasoning step for the tomato and onion salad mixture, which is intended to be savory and acidic.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding sugar instead of salt to the tomato and onion salad will ruin the flavor profile of the salad, making it sweet instead of savory, which clashes with the intended zingy lemon flavor and the savory kebab components.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action is performed directly into the bowl containing the salad mixture, committing the wrong ingredient to the recipe state.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the sugar is mixed into the diced tomatoes and onions, it cannot be removed, and the flavor balance is permanently altered.
mistake.why_plausible: Sugar and salt are both white, granular ingredients often stored in similar containers or nearby, making it a common human error to grab the wrong one when seasoning.

recipe_steps.text: Rinse lentils
Cut the squash into 2cm chunks and peel it
Wash the spring greens and slice them
Chop the onion
Fry the onion until golden (around 6-8 mins)
Add the squash and fry for 3 mins.
Add the spicy garlic & coconut paste to the pan and mix well.
Stir in the red lentils and the dhal spice mix.
Add the coconut milk and the ginger lentil stock pot along with 100ml of water and bring to the boil.
Cover with a lid, turn the heat down and let it simmer for 10 mins
Stir in the spring greens and then put the lid back on and cook for 5 more mins.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits the cooking medium to the pan before frying the onions, which is a fundamental step in the recipe.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using vinegar instead of sunflower oil will drastically alter the flavor profile of the curry, making it acidic and unsuitable for the intended dish.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring a liquid into the pan is a clear, observable commitment of an ingredient to the cooking vessel.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is poured into the hot pan, it will begin to evaporate and incorporate into the pan surface and any subsequent ingredients, making it impossible to remove without discarding the entire contents of the pan.
mistake.why_plausible: Bottles of oil and vinegar are often stored in similar locations in a kitchen, and a person might grab the wrong bottle if they are not paying close attention.

recipe_steps.text: Wash potatoes, peel and cut them into small cubes
Boil the potatoes for 15-20 mins or until soft, then drain.
Wash and slice the mushrooms
Peel and finely chop the onion
Cut the plant-based beef burger into thin strips
Toss the beef strips in half of the stroganoff seasoning
Heat a wide pan on high heat, add 2 tsps oil and sear the beef quickly on all sides. Remove and keep aside.
Reduce the heat, add a knob of butter, the onion and the rest of the stroganoff seasoning.  Cook for 5 mins until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 mins.
Mix in the tomato puree.
Stir in the mushroom stock pot and the cream. Gently bring to the boil then cook for 2 mins on low heat.
Mash the potatoes with some butter and the horseradish seasoning.
Return the beef (and its juices) to the sauce and cook for 2 mins, or longer for more 'well done' beef.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action introduces the cooking medium (oil) to the pan, which is essential for searing the plant-based beef strips.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using balsamic vinegar instead of sunflower oil will drastically alter the flavor profile of the Beef Stroganoff and will likely cause the plant-based beef to burn or stick to the pan rather than searing properly, as vinegar has a lower smoke point and different chemical properties than oil.
mistake.why_observable_now: The mistake happens at the exact moment the cooking medium is added to the pan, which is a key step before adding the beef.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is in the hot pan, it will evaporate or caramelize quickly, making it impossible to remove without cleaning the pan entirely and restarting the heating process.
mistake.why_plausible: Balsamic vinegar and sunflower oil bottles are often kept in similar storage areas, and a person might grab the wrong bottle in a hurry.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding liquid to the flour mixture is a key step in forming the dough; the type of liquid used fundamentally changes the dough's hydration and chemical properties.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using milk instead of water in a pizza dough recipe alters the texture, browning, and flavor profile, making it a different product than intended.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the liquid into the bowl is the moment the ingredient is committed to the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the milk is mixed into the flour, it cannot be removed, and the dough's consistency and chemistry are already altered.
mistake.why_plausible: Milk and water are both common liquids used in baking, and they look similar in a cup, making it a common procedural slip.

recipe_steps.text: Mix the flour with yeast, salt and water in a large bowl using a wooden spoon

Once the ingredients are roughly mixed, transfer the mixture onto the kitchen top and knead the dough by hand. This is done by rolling the dough on itself several times. Once the dough starts tearing, flatten the dough and fold the 4 edges to form a ball. Let the ball rest for a few minutes between repetitions.
Repeat the previous step several times until the dough is uniform and no longer sticks to the hands.
Split the dough in 2, then flatten and fold each chunk to form a ball.
Coat a plastic container with a little olive oil and place the dough balls in the container.
Let the pizza dough mature and rise for 24 hours in the fridge.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The action involves adding a liquid to the frying pan where the onions are about to be cooked, which is a key step in preparing the base of the Spanish omelette.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding vinegar instead of olive oil will drastically alter the flavor profile and cooking properties of the onions, ruining the intended taste and texture of the omelette.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring a liquid into the pan is a direct commitment of an ingredient to the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is poured into the pan and mixed with the onions, it is impossible to remove it without discarding the entire batch of ingredients.
mistake.why_plausible: Vinegar bottles and olive oil bottles are often stored in similar containers and kept in the same area near the hob, making it a realistic mistake to grab the wrong one.

Add the oil and the salt, mixing everything well. The quantities are fairly loose: just make sure the leaves are coated and sprinkle with a bit of salt.
Cook for 15 minutes in an oven preheated at 180 degrees with the fan on (200 if the oven does not have a fan). Once it's mainly wilted but crisp at the edges, it's ready.

goal: prepare Pizza with Aubergine and Egg

recipe_steps.text: Wash the aubergine and chop it in 2cm cubes
Fry the aubergine with sunflower oil until it's very soft. Add salt and black pepper while cooking.
When the aubergine is ready, move it to a plate with kitchen towel to absorb the oil
Hard-boil the egg in a saucepan for 5 minutes
Peel the egg and slice it in 4 slices

Stretch the pizza dough using the semolina flour to avoid the dough getting stuck on the hands and surfaces. To stretch the dough, first press it with the fingertips, starting from the centre towards the edges, rotating and repeating until it no longer stretches. Then transfer the dough to the back of both hands and slowly rotate and stretch the dough until it reaches the desired size.
Add some semolina flour to the pizza peel, then add the dough on top of it and add all toppings to the pizza: tomato sauce first, then mozzarella, finally aubergine and egg.
Transfer the pizza to the pre-heated pizza oven and cook for 5 minutes. Rotate the pizza halfway through to ensure the pizza is cooked evenly.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding the cooking fat is a key step to prepare the base for the tomato sauce, and the choice of ingredient directly impacts the flavor profile of the final dish.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using balsamic vinegar instead of olive oil to stir-fry garlic will result in a sharp, acidic, and caramelized flavor that is completely inappropriate for a standard tomato sauce base, ruining the intended taste of the pizza.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action involves pouring a liquid ingredient directly into the cooking vessel, which is a clear commitment to the recipe state.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the balsamic vinegar is in the hot pan with the garlic, it will immediately reduce and coat the garlic, making it impossible to remove or neutralize without discarding the entire base and starting over.
mistake.why_plausible: Balsamic vinegar and olive oil bottles are often stored in similar containers or locations in a kitchen, making it a common slip to grab the wrong one while preparing to cook.

goal: prepare Pizza with Plant-Based Mince and Mushrooms

recipe_steps.text: Wash the mushrooms and slice them thinly
Stir fry the mushrooms in a pan with sunflower oil. Add black pepper and garlic powder while cooking.

Stretch the pizza dough using the semolina flour to avoid the dough getting stuck on the hands and surfaces. To stretch the dough first press it with the fingertips, starting from the centre towards the edges, rotating and repeating until it no longer stretches. Then transfer the dough to the back of both hands and slowly rotate and stretch the dough until it reaches the desired size.

Add some semolina flour to the pizza peel, then add the dough on top of it and add all toppings to the pizza: tomato sauce first, then mozzarella, finally mushrooms and the pre-cooked plant-based mince.
Transfer the pizza to the pre-heated pizza oven and cook for 5 minutes. Rotate the pizza halfway through to ensure the pizza is cooked evenly.

Season to taste and serve.

goal: prepare Aloo Stuffing for Masala Dosa

recipe_steps.text: Wash and boil the cut potato halves in a pressure cooker. Once it is cooled, peel it and smash it. Also, keep all other ingredients ready.

Take a frying pan on medium heat, add 4tbsp of olive oil and mustard seeds. Once the mustard starts spluttering, add urad dal into the pan. Saute it for a while. When the urad dal turns brown add slit green chili`, and grated ginger. Saute it for few seconds.

Then add chopped onion, along with 1 tbsp oil and salt and then continue frying until the onions turn soft. Add turmeric powder, saute for a few seconds. Remove the pan from the heat and allow contents to cool.
Now add smashed potato to the pan and mix until finely blended. Once it is mixed, add salt to taste. Garnish with coriander leaves.
The aloo stuffing is ready to be served.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Add the turmeric powder in the spoon into the pan over the left burner of the electric hob.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding mustard seeds to hot oil is a foundational step for tempering (tadka) in Indian cooking, which requires specific timing and order.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding turmeric powder at this stage instead of mustard seeds ruins the tempering process, as turmeric can burn quickly in hot oil and the mustard seeds are missing, which are essential for the flavor profile of the aloo stuffing.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action involves committing an ingredient directly into the cooking vessel (the pan with hot oil).
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the turmeric is added to hot oil, it disperses and begins to fry, making it impossible to remove or separate from the oil.
mistake.why_plausible: The cook has both mustard seeds and turmeric powder packets nearby on the counter, and it is a common slip to grab the wrong packet or spoon while multitasking.

actions.original_text: With the right hand, tip the cup over the bowl of dosa batter to add some more water into the batter. This is done because the dosa batter seemed too thick for making dosas. So adding a little bit of water will make it the right consistency.

mistake.original_action_text: With the right hand, tip the cup over the bowl of dosa batter to add some more water into the batter. This is done because the dosa batter seemed too thick for making dosas. So adding a little bit of water will make it the right consistency.
mistake.llm_original_action_text: With the right hand, tip the cup over the bowl of dosa batter to add some more water into the batter. This is done because the dosa batter seemed too thick for making dosas. So adding a little bit of water will make it the right consistency.
mistake.mistake_action_text: With the right hand, tip the cup over the bowl of dosa batter to add some milk into the batter. This is done because the dosa batter seemed too thick for making dosas. So adding a little bit of milk will make it the right consistency.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding liquid to the dosa batter is a critical step to adjust its consistency for proper spreading on the pan.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Dosa batter is fermented rice and lentil batter; adding milk instead of water will alter the flavor, texture, and fermentation properties, ruining the traditional savory outcome of the masala dosa.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the liquid into the batter is directly observable as it changes the composition of the mixture.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the milk is mixed into the entire bowl of batter, it cannot be removed, and the chemical/flavor profile of the batter is permanently altered.
mistake.why_plausible: It is a common mistake to reach for a similar-looking white liquid container or to misidentify the contents of a cup when trying to adjust the consistency of a batter quickly.

recipe_steps.text: Set 200g of basmati rice aside
Slice 1 medium onion and slit few green chilies. Grate ginger and few cloves of garlic.
Add the chilli, garlic and ginger into a kitchen mortar and crush them together into a paste using a pestle.

Pour 5 tbsp of olive oil, and 1 tbsp of ghee into to a pressure cooker placed on medium heat. When the oil/ghee mixture becomes hot, add the spices (bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, anise flower etc) and cashew nuts to it and saute for a few minutes allowing them to fry. Once the cashews turn slightly golden brown, add chopped onions and fry it for a while. Then add the spice paste from the mortar into the cooker and saute the mixture.

After a few minutes, add garam masala powder to the cooker and continue to saute until mixed well. Salt maybe added. Then add green peas into the cooker and stir fry for a few minutes under medium heat.
Add 300ml of water and 1tbsp of lemon juice followed by the drained basmati rice and fry on a slightly high flame for 2 to 3 minutes. Mix gently to evenly coat the rice with the cooked masala.
Cover the pressure cooker and place the whistle. Pressure cook for 2 whistles on a medium high flame. Turn off and remove from the stove. Leaving it on the hot burner will further cook the rice
When the pressure drops naturally, open the lid and fluff the peas pulao. The peas pulao is then ready to serve.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding the cooking fat (olive oil) is a fundamental step for sauteing the spices and aromatics in the pressure cooker.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Vinegar has a sharp, acidic flavor profile that will clash significantly with the spices and aromatics of the Peas Pulao, ruining the intended savory and aromatic balance of the dish.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action involves committing an ingredient to the cooking vessel, which is a key procedural step.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is added to the hot pressure cooker and mixed with the spices, it cannot be removed, and its acidity will permeate the entire dish.
mistake.why_plausible: Vinegar and olive oil are both liquid condiments often stored in similar bottles in a kitchen, making it a realistic slip during a busy cooking process.

goal: prepare Chickpea and Spinach Curry with Rice

recipe_steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy bottomed pan; make sure you have a lid for it.
Add the onions and when they start to sizzle add the whole spices and chillies. Cook on a low heat until the onions are starting to brown.
Add the garlic and finger chillies to the pan and cook for a minute more.
If the oil has disappeared add a little more, you need the oil to cook the ground spices out.
Add the curry Masala or ground spices to the pan and continue to cook on a low heat for 45 seconds
Add the diluted tomato puree, stir in and cook for 30 seconds or so.

Add the tomatoes, mango chutney and salt, stir in and bring to a simmer. Turn the heat to the lowest you can (a heat diffuser on gas works a treat) and put the lid on. Leave to cook for around 20 minutes.
Take the lid off and stir. If it looks a little dry add a splash of water. Add the Garam Masala. Stir in and put the lid back on. Leave to cook for another 15 minutes.

After 15 minutes remove the lid and stir. If you like a thick sauce you may want to turn the heat up now and let it reduce down. If the sauce looks a little oily for your taste you can use a ladle to skim some of the oil off.
Add the chickpeas and spinach, and later add the coconut milk and the juice of half a lemon. Season to taste.
Add some coconut milk and a squeeze of lemon, to taste
Stir in the fresh coriander and serve over plain boiled rice with a chapatti or roti.

recipe_steps.text: Put a large pan of salted water on to boil, and add the pasta
Optionally add garlic, then pound in a pestle and mortar with a pinch of sea salt.
Pick, roughly chop and add the basil leaves, then bash to a paste (or pulse in a food processor).
Add the pine nuts (very lightly toast first, if you like) to the mixture and pound again, then stir in half the Parmesan.
Drizzle in some oil - you need just enough to bind the sauce and get it to an oozy consistency.
Add most of the remaining cheese, then season to perfection with salt and black pepper. Have a taste, and keep adding a bit more cheese or oil until you are happy with the taste and consistency.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice at the end to give it a little twang, if you like, but it's not essential.
Add frozen peas to the pasta with 4 minutes left.
Combine the salad ingredients in a bowl with the oil and vinegar.
Drain the pasta when al dente, and add the pesto.

mistake.why_plausible: The person is handling both pasta and peas in the same session, and it is a common slip to grab the wrong bag when both are sitting on the counter.

mistake.original_action_text: Pour pasta into boiling water with both hands.
mistake.llm_original_action_text: Pour pasta into boiling water with both hands.
mistake.mistake_action_text: Pour the entire bag of frozen peas into the boiling water with both hands.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits the primary starch component (pasta) to the boiling water, which is a fundamental step in the recipe.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: By adding frozen peas instead of the pasta, the main component of the Carbonara dish is missing, and the boiling water is now contaminated with a large volume of peas that will overcook and disintegrate before the pasta could even be added.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring ingredients into the boiling water is a clear, high-stakes commitment point in the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the frozen peas are poured into the boiling water, they cannot be easily retrieved or separated from the water, and the water will be ruined for cooking the pasta.
mistake.why_plausible: The person is holding a bag of pasta and a bag of peas, and it is a common slip to grab the wrong bag when both are being prepared for the same meal.

recipe_steps.text: Break the chocolate into fairly evenly sized pieces - I find the easiest and most satisfying way to start this process is to leave it in the packet, or put it in a resealable bag, give it a good whack against the work surface, then chop up any large pieces that remain. Cut the butter into chunky dice.

Leave the butter and chocolate to melt together, stirring now and then to encourage them along. Once you have a smooth, well-blended mixture, turn off the heat, lift the bowl off the pan (remember that it will be hot) and pour the mixture into a cold bowl or jug to cool slightly while you prepare the rest of the batter.

Put the egg and egg yolk in a large bowl with the sugar and a pinch of salt. Vigorously whisk by hand or with electric beaters, until the mixture is pale yellow and voluminous. Very gently fold in the melted chocolate mixture with a large metal spoon, taking care not to knock too much air out of the batter. Repeat with the flour.

Grease the insides of two small ramekins or pudding moulds with butter, put the cocoa in one, and turn and tip to coat the insides, holding it over the other ramekin to catch any powder. Tip the rest of the cocoa into the second ramekin and repeat.

Divide the batter between the two moulds, leaving a little room at the top for them to rise. If you'd like to eat them immediately, put them on the hot baking tray in the oven for 12 minutes, until the tops are set and the cake mix is just starting to come away from the sides of the moulds.
