mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action involves transferring the prepared batter into the ramekins for baking.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: The user is supposed to transfer the chocolate pudding batter, but instead transfers a different mixture (likely the raw egg/sugar base before the chocolate was folded in), which will result in a failed pudding structure and flavor profile.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action is the direct commitment of the batter into the cooking vessel.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the wrong mixture is spooned into the ramekins, it is mixed with the butter/cocoa coating, making it impossible to separate or correct without discarding the entire batch.
mistake.why_plausible: The user has multiple bowls on the counter and could easily confuse the bowl containing the chocolate batter with a bowl containing a different component or a previous stage of the mixture.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Pour sesame oil into the pan with my left hand.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The choice of oil is critical for stir-frying at high temperatures; using an oil with a low smoke point will burn and ruin the flavor profile of the dish.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Sesame oil has a low smoke point and a very strong, distinct flavor that will dominate the stir-fry and turn bitter when heated to the high temperatures required for this recipe.
mistake.why_observable_now: The mistake is committed the moment the oil is poured into the hot pan, as the smoke point will be reached almost immediately.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the oil is in the pan and heated, it cannot be removed without discarding the entire batch of oil and potentially cleaning the pan, which is difficult once the cooking process has begun.
mistake.why_plausible: Sesame oil is a common ingredient in Asian cooking and is often stored near other cooking oils, making it a realistic slip for a cook to grab the wrong bottle.

recipe_steps.text: Mix the uttapam pancake mix into water in a bowl until a smooth batter is prepared and set it aside for 10-15 minutes.
Wash tomato, coriander, and onions in fresh running water and chop tomato and onion into small pieces.
Take a frying pan and place it on gas stove to heat it up. Place some butter on the heated pan and spread it on the whole pan in a circular motion.
When the pan is hot enough, pour a ladle full of batter in the centre of the pan. At this stage the pan has to be hot otherwise the batter won't rise and the uttapams will be flat.
Do not spread the batter too much, uthappam has to be made thick. If the batter doesn't spread on its own, then you may lightly spread a bit. Lower the flame.
Place the chopped onions and tomato on the pancake in the pan and flip the sides of the pancake on the lower flame.
Add oil or ghee around the edges and allow to cook on a low to medium flame until the base cooks well and firms up.
Sprinkle little oil over the onions and turn to the other side. Put some more butter on the sides of the pancake in the pan, so that it does not stick to the sides of the pan.
Cook until the onions are done. The color of the uthappam depends on the temperature of the batter & the pan. Usually batter straight away from fridge does not yield golden uthappam.
Make sure it is cooked well from inside. If you like caramelized onions, you may cook longer. To make the next uttapam, ensure the pan is hot enough.
Cook both the sides of the pancake on a lower flame until fully cooked. Garnish it with some coriander and tomato ketchup.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The liquid used to hydrate the dry pancake mix determines the consistency and flavor profile of the batter.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Uttapam is a savory fermented pancake traditionally made with water; using milk will alter the texture, prevent proper fermentation/browning, and change the flavor profile significantly, making it more like a sweet crepe batter.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the liquid into the dry mix is the point where the ingredient is committed to the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the milk is mixed into the dry batter, it cannot be removed or separated, and the chemical properties of the batter are permanently altered.
mistake.why_plausible: Milk and water are both common liquids used in various pancake recipes, and it is a common slip to grab the wrong container if both are present on the counter.

recipe_steps.text: Fill a cup with whole milk and heat it in the microwave for 3-4 minutes. Stir the heated milk with a milk frother to make the cappuccino frothier.
Take another empty cup and put 2 teaspoons of sugar and coffee in the cup. Add 2 teaspoons of water and slowly add more until the ingredients are just wet so that you can beat the mixture.
Add more water if needed, whipping it vigorously with the spoon.
Once the mixture in nicely thickened, smooth, and almost shiny, your Indian whipped coffee is mixture is ready.
Pour the heated milk in the golden-brown paste and stir it well until all ingredients are uniformly mixed. Heat the cappuccino again in microwave for 30 seconds and it is ready to drink.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action is the final assembly step where the heated milk is combined with the prepared coffee paste to create the cappuccino.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Pouring water instead of the heated milk into the coffee paste will result in a watery, diluted coffee drink rather than a creamy cappuccino, failing the core recipe requirement of mixing the milk with the paste.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring is a direct commitment of the liquid into the cup containing the coffee paste, which is immediately visible as the wrong liquid consistency and color.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the water is poured into the coffee paste, the mixture is already diluted and the paste structure is compromised, making it impossible to separate or fix without starting the entire coffee preparation over.
mistake.why_plausible: The person has both water and milk containers on the table, and it is a common procedural slip to grab the wrong container when performing a repetitive pouring task.

recipe_steps.text: Chop half of the onion into smaller pieces and other half into larger bits. Chop the tomatoes into smaller pieces and grind them in a grinder with fresh garlic and green chillies to make a smooth tomato puree. Chop some green chillies into pieces and add them into the puree.
In a large kadai or any other pan, now melt butter with oil on medium heat. Add cumin seeds to the melted butter.
Add the chopped onion and saute for 3 minutes until softened. Then add the sliced green chili and ginger garlic paste and saute for another 1 to 2 minutes.

Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, red chilli powder, and salt to the mixture and saute the mixture uniformly. Then add 1/2 cup water and stir. Wait for the whole mixture to homogenise.
Add the tomato puree to the mixture in the pan and mix it thoroughly. Cook the puree for about 5 minutes on a low flame or until the butter separates out from the mixture.
Add the pieces of cottage cheese in the mixture and cook it for 5-10 minutes on a low flame. Cover the pan or kadai with a lid and cook for 5 to 6 minutes on medium heat.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action introduces the primary cooking fat (butter) to the pan, which is essential for sauteing the aromatics and spices for the Kadhai Paneer base.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Replacing butter with sugar will cause the sugar to caramelize and burn in the hot pan, ruining the flavor profile of the dish and preventing the proper sauteing of the onions and spices.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of placing the ingredient into the pan is a direct, observable commitment of a substance to the cooking vessel.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once sugar is melted and caramelized in a hot pan, it cannot be removed without discarding the entire contents of the pan and cleaning it, as it will stick and burn.
mistake.why_plausible: Sugar and butter containers or portions can look similar if stored in similar bowls or containers on the countertop, leading to a common procedural slip.

recipe_steps.text: Wash and rinse urad dal (whole black lentil) and rajma (kidney beans) in a large bowl. Soak in 3 cups water overnight.

In the morning, drain the water in which the dal and rajma was soaked. Transfer the dal and rajma to a pressure cooker with 1 teaspoon salt. Add around 3.5 cups water. Cook in the pressure cooker on high-medium heat for 10 whistles, then lower the heat to low-medium and cook for another 10 minutes. In total around 15 to 20 whistles.

Let the pressure release naturally. The dal and rajma should be completely cooked, and you should be able to mash them with your fingers. If using the Instant pot, pressure cook the lentils on high pressure for 30 minutes with natural pressure release.
Take a frying pan and place it on gas stove to heat it up. Add some butter in the pan and wait for it to melt. Add 1 tablespoon of cumin seeds to the melted butter.

Add chopped onions to the pan. Cook the onion for around 6 to 7 minutes or until it turns light golden brown. Keep stirring it continuously so that it doesn't burn and keep heat on medium. Add chopped tomato to the pan and saute them with onions.

Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, red chilli powder, and salt to the mixture and saute the mixture uniformly. Cook for 2 minutes or until the puree mixes well with masala and oil starts oozing out from the sides.

Add the boiled kidney beans and black urad pulses along with the broth to the mixture and mix it thoroughly. Add 1/2 cup water, stir, and set heat to low. Cook the Dal makhani for 5-10 minutes on a low flame.
For boiled rice, fill an empty glass with rice and wash it three times in the fresh running water.
Take a pressure cooker and add the washed rice into it. Add 1.5 glass of water with the rice. Close the lid of the pressure cooker and boil the rice for 5 minutes on a high flame.
After 5 minutes, turn off the flame and put the pressure cooker aside for 5 more minutes for boiled rice. Add the dal makhani to the boiled rice and it is ready to serve.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action involves transferring the prepared aromatics (onions) into a vessel. The recipe requires these to be sautéed in a frying pan with butter and spices before being added to the dal.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding raw onions directly into the pressure cooker (which already contains the cooked dal) instead of sautéing them in a separate pan prevents the development of the necessary flavor base (the masala) and results in raw, crunchy onions in a dish that should have a smooth, creamy texture.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of transferring the onions is a distinct, observable step that deviates from the intended recipe flow.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the raw onions are mixed into the cooked dal in the pressure cooker, they cannot be removed or sautéed properly, ruining the texture and flavor profile of the Dal Makhani.
mistake.why_plausible: The cook is managing multiple vessels and ingredients simultaneously; it is a plausible slip to move the prepared ingredient into the wrong container while distracted by the ongoing prep work.

recipe_steps.text: In a large bowl, add 2 cups whole wheat flour (atta). Make a well in the centre. Add 1 tablespoon oil or ghee, and roughly 1/3 to 1/2 cup water.
Bring the mixture together and knead into a smooth, soft dough for a few minutes. Add more water if needed.
Pinch two small balls from the dough. Flatten them and dust with whole wheat flour.
With a rolling pin, roll them into rounds roughly 4 to 5 inches in diameter. Try making both the discs the same size.
On one of the discs, place the potato stuffing in the centre, keeping about 1-inch empty space from the sides.
Gently place the second circle on top. Press and seal the edges with your fingertips. If you are not able to seal the edges, then brush or spread some water on the edges and then seal.
Dust some flour on the stuffed aloo ka paratha and start rolling.
Roll the paratha into a roundabout 7 to 8 inches in diameter, or about the size of a normal roti or chapati.
On a hot tawa (skillet or griddle), place the rolled paratha. The tawa should be quite hot; cooking parathas at a low flame will harden them. Ideally, the finished parathas are crisp as well as soft.
When the base is partly cooked, flip the paratha using a spatula. You will see some air pockets on this side.
Spread some butter on the partly cooked part.
Flip again and you will see nice golden blisters on the second side. To clarify, the side which has been spread with ghee will be on the bottom.
This side has to be cooked more than the previous side.
Spread some butter on the second side facing you. A well-made and well-roasted aloo paratha will always puff up when roasting.

Flip again once or twice till both sides are cooked properly, with crisp brown spots. You should also press the aloo paratha edges down with a spatula or spoon so that they are fried well. Repeat, making all parathas this way.

recipe_steps.text: Break open 2 eggs in a mixing bowl, then add red chilli powder along with required salt.
Chop an onion into smaller pieces and add it to the whisked eggs.
Heat a pan with butter when it is hot - pour the egg mixture on it. Tilt it so that the egg mixture is even on all the edges.
Take a bread slice dip in the egg then flip over and place it. Repeat this for the other egg too. So, the dipped side should come on top. Drizzle oil or butter.
Once it gets cooked on one side and flip over to other side and press it with the ladle. Cook for 2 mins then flip over and serve.

recipe_steps.text: Fill a cup with whole milk and heat it in the microwave for 3-4 minutes. Stir the heated milk with a milk frother to make the cappuccino frothier.

Take another empty cup and put 2 teaspoons of sugar and coffee in the cup. Add about a half tablespoon of water and slowly add more until the ingredients are just wet so that you can beat the mixture.

Once the mixture in nicely thickened, smooth, and almost shiny, your cappuccino mixture is ready
Pour the heated milk in the golden-brown paste and stir it well until all ingredients are uniformly mixed. Heat the cappuccino again in microwave for 30 seconds and it is ready to drink.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Setting the microwave timer is a critical step to ensure the milk reaches the correct temperature for a cappuccino without boiling over or scalding.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Setting the timer to 10 minutes instead of 3-4 minutes will cause the milk to boil over, spill inside the microwave, and likely burn, ruining the milk and potentially damaging the microwave.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of setting the timer is a direct, observable interaction with the microwave interface that immediately precedes the heating process.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the milk has boiled over and burned inside the microwave, the milk is unusable, and the microwave will require significant cleaning, making it impossible to continue the recipe without starting over.
mistake.why_plausible: It is a common human error to misread or misset a dial or digital timer on an appliance, especially when distracted.

recipe_steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Rinse the chickpeas, then place the chickpeas on a towel and lightly towel dry them so they aren't wet from rinsing. You can remove any loose skins at this time too.

Place the chickpeas on a baking sheet and drizzle with the olive oil. Toss to coat, then sprinkle with the paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper. Stir the chickpeas and shake the pan a few times to distribute the seasoning. Put the tray in the oven and roast the chickpeas for 15 minutes.
Take apart the head of lettuce. Wash the lettuce leaves and squeeze to dry.
Stir the chickpeas and roast for 10 to 15 more minutes
Tear the lettuce and place it in a large bowl.
Wash the tomatoes and then cut them in half.
Add the tomatoes to the bowl
Chop the cucumber into small pieces and add it to the bowl.
Drain the olives, tear them in half and add them to the bowl.
Crumble the blue cheese into the bowl.
Stir the ingredients in the bowl together to mix.
Remove the chickpeas from the oven and discard any burnt chickpeas.
Mix the salad and the chickpeas together in a bowl to serve.

recipe_steps.text: Put dried mushrooms into a large bowl.
Finely chop the onions.
Pour boiling water over the dried mushrooms, stir and soak.
Measure out the pre-chopped garlic.
Wash and chop the fresh chestnut and shiitake mushrooms.
Drain the dried mushrooms into a pan, keeping the liquid.
Crumble vegetable stock cube into the mushroom liquid, then squeeze the mushrooms gently with a fork to remove any liquid.

Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a shallow saucepan or deep frying pan over a medium flame. Add the pre-chopped garlic and the finely chopped onion into the pan, then fry for about 5 mins until soft, stirring regularly.
Measure out the risotto rice.
Stir in chopped chestnut mushrooms, chopped shiitake mushrooms, and the dried mushrooms
Season with salt and pepper and continue to cook, stirring regularly, for 8 mins until the fresh mushrooms have softened.
Tip risotto rice into the pan and cook for 1 min. Pour over a glass of white wine and let it bubble to nothing so the alcohol evaporates.
Keep the pan over a medium heat and pour in a quarter of the mushroom stock. Simmer the rice, stirring often, until the rice has absorbed all the liquid.

Add about the same amount of stock again and continue to simmer and stir - it should start to become creamy, plump and tender. By the time the final quarter of stock is added, the rice should be almost cooked.
Grate the cheese.
Continue stirring and add the rest of the stock.

When the rice is cooked take the pan off the heat, add butter and scatter over grated parmesan or Grana Padano cheese and tear and scatter a handful of parsley leaves. Chop the rest of the parsley and save for later.
Give the risotto a final stir, add more parsley and taste.

mistake.mistake_action_text: pour the vinegar into the glass measuring jug
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The wine is a key liquid component for deglazing the pan and providing acidity to the risotto; replacing it with vinegar fundamentally alters the flavor profile of the dish.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Vinegar is significantly more acidic and pungent than white wine, which will ruin the delicate balance of the mushroom risotto, making it unpalatable.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the liquid into the measuring jug is a direct commitment of the ingredient to the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is poured into the jug and subsequently added to the hot pan with the rice and mushrooms, it cannot be removed or neutralized without discarding the entire batch.
mistake.why_plausible: Vinegar and white wine are often stored in similar bottles or locations in a kitchen, and a cook might grab the wrong bottle in a moment of distraction.

recipe_steps.text: To make this salad, start by preparing the dressing. Whisk the dressing ingredients together, in a small bowl, until they're fully combined. Taste and add additional seasonings, if desired.
Next, chop your cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, carrot, coriander, and red onion, and add them to a large bowl alongside the beans and diced tomatoes.
Toss to combine, then pour the dressing on top and toss once more until the salad ingredients are fully coated in the dressing.
Slice piece of sourdough bread and place on side of bowl.
Serve immediately and enjoy!

recipe_steps.text: Crack the eggs into a medium bowl. Whisk until smooth and combined, with no streaks of egg white remaining.
Spray olive oil in a small nonstick skillet. Bring to medium heat.
Add chopped red onions and finger chillies to a pan and saute until soft
Pour in the eggs, and let them cook for a few seconds without stirring. Pull a rubber spatula across the bottom of the pan to form large, soft curds of scrambled eggs.

Continue cooking over medium-low heat, folding and stirring the eggs every few seconds. Scrape the spatula along the bottom and sides of the pan often to form more curds and to prevent any part of the eggs from drying out
Remove the pan from the heat when the eggs are mostly set, but a little liquid egg remains. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add cottage cheese to plate and season to taste with salt, pepper, oregano and olive oil.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits a specific ingredient (salad seeds) into the main salad bowl, which is a key component of the Tabbouleh recipe.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Replacing the salad seeds with salt significantly alters the flavor profile and texture of the dish, potentially making it inedible due to excessive saltiness.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action involves the physical transfer of an ingredient into the mixing bowl, which is a visible and irreversible step in the assembly process.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the salt is mixed into the salad bowl with the other ingredients, it cannot be easily removed or separated, ruining the batch.
mistake.why_plausible: The salt shaker and the salad seeds were both handled near the scale, making it a realistic human error to grab the wrong container while distracted by the scale.

Place salmon teriyaki skewers on a baking sheet. Roast for 11 to 15 minutes, until just cooked. Set aside until cool enough to handle.
Pre-heat air fryer to 180 degrees C
Place broccoli in air fryer and roast for 15 minutes. Season with oil, salt, pepper, oregano, and garlic granules half-way through.
Add pre-made Chickpea, Spinach & Quinoa salad to plate.
Add broccoli and salmon skewers to plate ontop of salad. Serve and enjoy!

mistake.mistake_action_text: With the left hand, adjust the temperature of the oven by turning the knob to the left to 100 degrees Celsius.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: The oven temperature is a critical parameter for roasting the salmon skewers to ensure they are cooked through within the specified time frame.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Setting the oven to 100 degrees Celsius is significantly lower than the required 180 degrees Celsius, meaning the salmon will not cook properly within the 11-15 minute window, leading to undercooked fish.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action is performed directly on the oven control knob, which is the primary interface for setting the cooking temperature.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the oven is set to a low temperature, the salmon will not reach the necessary internal temperature for safe consumption, and simply increasing the heat later will likely result in uneven cooking or a dry exterior.
mistake.why_plausible: It is a common procedural slip to turn a knob in the wrong direction or misread the temperature dial when adjusting settings quickly.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits a prepared ingredient to a cooking vessel, which is a final step in integrating components into the recipe.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding raw red pepper to the boiling pasta water ruins the texture of the pepper and interferes with the pasta cooking process, which is intended to be a separate component of the salad.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of scraping ingredients into a vessel is a clear, irreversible commitment of the ingredient to the cooking medium.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the pepper pieces are in the boiling water, they will soften and disperse, making it impossible to remove them without discarding the entire batch of pasta.
mistake.why_plausible: The salad bowl and the pot of boiling pasta are both on the counter, and it is a common slip to misidentify the target container when performing repetitive tasks.

recipe_steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees C
Place fishcakes on baking tray and place in over for 30 minutes
Place frozen broccoli and green beans to air fryer for 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper half-way through.
Boil water for couscous (170 ml)
Add couscous and boiling water to pot (no flame needed), leave until water has been absorbed
Slice onion, chili pepper, and bell pepper and place to side
Add oil to a nonstick pan. Bring to medium heat.
Once warm, add garlic, onions, red peppers and chilis to pan. Cook until browned
Add broccoli and green beans to pan and stir
Season pan with salt, pepper, and sesame oil
Serve fishcakes on top of couscous with side of vegetables

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding seasoning is a final, irreversible step that directly impacts the flavor profile of the dish.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding sugar to a savory vegetable stir-fry instead of salt will ruin the flavor balance and make the dish unpalatable.

mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the sugar is mixed into the hot vegetables, it cannot be removed, and the entire batch of vegetables would likely need to be discarded.
mistake.why_plausible: Sugar and salt shakers often look similar or are stored in the same area, making it a common procedural slip to grab the wrong one.

recipe_steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the onion softens.
Add the garlic and chilli peppers and cook for a further minute.
Add the minced beef and cook for 5-6 minutes, until browned. Stir often, breaking up any large chunks of meat with a spatula.
Add the carrot, celery, bell peppers, and mushrooms and cook for a further 2-3 minutes.
Add the tomato pasta sauce, oregano, tinned tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Stir and bring to the boil. Turn down the heat and simmer for 15 -20 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, boil a large pan of salted water. Add the spaghetti and cook for 10-12 minutes until al dente.
Drain the spaghetti and divide it between bowls.
Spoon the Bolognese on top of the spaghetti and sprinkle on parmesan before serving.

recipe_steps.text: Cut the cucumber lengthwise down the middle then into 2.4cm/1 inch pieces

Salt 30 minutes - Put them in a bowl then toss with salt. Leave for 30 minutes. The salt will draw out water from the cucumbers which dilutes flavour when you eat them. It also seasons the cucumbers all the way though.

Drain and discard the cucumber water from the bowl (too salty to re-use for another purpose). Use a colander if you want to be thorough else just drain it out of the bowl, using your hand to hold the cucumbers in.
Whisk the soy sauce and sesame oil in a bowl until it combines properly. You'll know because it becomes murky and thicker, rather than clear and split.

Add 2 teaspoons of chilli crisp - or more if you dare! You want to get a mound of the crispy chilli - it will be well soaked with the red chilli oil that colours this salad. You can always add more after you toss. Taste and add, taste and add!
Finally grate and add ginger and garlic to bowl. Toss well then pile up high into a shallow bowl and serve!

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits the primary protein to the curry base, which is a fundamental step in the recipe.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: The recipe specifically calls for chicken; substituting it with raw pork changes the dish entirely and requires different cooking times and flavor profiles, making it no longer a Thai Red Chicken Curry.
mistake.why_observable_now: The substitution happens at the exact moment the protein is added to the pot, which is the point of no return.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the raw pork is mixed into the hot curry paste and oil, it cannot be removed without discarding the entire base of the curry.
mistake.why_plausible: It is a common kitchen error to grab the wrong bowl of prepped meat if they are stored similarly in the fridge or on the counter.

recipe_steps.text: In separate pots, boil the chicken and potatoes until cooked through.
Once boiled, drain out any excess water from the potatoes and then mash them.
Once boiled, shred the chicken.
Mix all seasoning along with the shredded chicken until well combined.
Mix the shredded chicken, mashed potatoes and cheese together.

Scoop some of the mixture and roll in your palms to make a smooth ball. (adjust the quantity of the scooped mixture to obtain your preferred size; repeat this process until all the mixture has been used)
Dredge each Chicken-cheese ball into flour, then dip into egg and roll in the breadcrumbs, ensuring the entire surface of the chicken ball is covered in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil over medium heat, about 2-inch deep to cover the balls halfway at least.
Gently add the chicken cheese balls into the oil, ensuring the pan does not get overcrowded. Fry the balls until golden turning as required to cook through and brown evenly.

mistake.mistake_action_text: Using both my hands to pour some salt from the bag into the jar on the counter surface.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits the ingredient to the sugar jar, which is then used to sweeten the hibiscus drink.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Adding salt instead of sugar will ruin the flavor profile of the hibiscus drink, making it unpalatable.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the ingredient into the jar is the point where the contamination is introduced into the supply.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the salt is mixed into the sugar jar, it is impossible to separate them, effectively ruining the entire batch of sugar.
mistake.why_plausible: Sugar and salt are both white, granular substances often stored in similar containers or bags, making them easy to confuse during a repetitive task.

recipe_steps.text: Heat oil in a pan and throw in some cinnamon sticks, cardamon, cloves, black peppercorn.
Add half of the sliced onion and fry until the onion begin to brown. Set aside the other half for later use.
Add water to the mix along with turmeric and red chili powder and stir.
Then add in the garlic and ginger paste, ghee, yoghurt and stir.
Now add the meat to the mix and stir to mix evenly.
Cover and cook until the meat is cooked through and a bit tender (50 - 55mins), occasionally adding water and stirring to prevent burning and sticking to the pan
Fry the second half of the onions until browned. Once cooked, add to the rest of the mixture.
Once the meat is cooked and tender, add the fried onion, cumin, garam masala, ghee and chili and cook through until the meat is tender.

mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: Adding the correct spice (garam masala) is essential for the flavor profile of the Mangsho Bhuna, as it is a key aromatic component added at this stage.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using cinnamon powder instead of garam masala significantly alters the intended spice balance and flavor profile of the dish, making it taste incorrect.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the spice into the saucepan is a direct commitment of the ingredient to the main cooking vessel.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the powder is mixed into the sauce and meat, it cannot be removed or separated, permanently altering the dish's flavor.
mistake.why_plausible: Cinnamon powder and garam masala are both brown, finely ground spices often stored in similar-looking containers, making it easy to grab the wrong one during a busy cooking process.

recipe_steps.text: Peel and slice mangoes.
Add mangoes, ice cubes, cold water, honey, coconut milk, and yogurt to blender.
Blend on high until smooth, approx. 2 - 3 min.
Slice and peel remaining mango, add to the blender and blend to combine, approx. 30 secs-1 min. Enjoy.

mistake.mistake_action_text: pouring the bottle of vinegar into the saucepan using my right hand.
mistake.why_this_action_is_critical: This action commits a liquid to the saucepan where the potatoes are being fried, which is a fundamental step in the cooking process.
mistake.why_goal_breaking: Using vinegar instead of oil will completely ruin the flavor profile of the French fries and prevent them from frying properly, as vinegar has a different boiling point and chemical composition.
mistake.why_observable_now: The action of pouring the liquid into the pan is a direct, observable commitment of an ingredient to the recipe.
mistake.why_hard_to_recover: Once the vinegar is mixed with the potatoes and heated, it cannot be removed, and the potatoes will have absorbed the acidic flavor, making them inedible as French fries.
mistake.why_plausible: Bottles of oil and vinegar are often stored in similar containers in a kitchen, making it a common slip to grab the wrong one while distracted.
